title: “The job I eventually will have has not been invented yet”: Reflections on Being an IT Specialist and Librarian
content:
Today’s guest post is from Barak Stussman, an IT Specialist at the Library of Congress. Barak has worked at the Library of Congress for the past 28 years, supporting both information technology colleagues and librarians. As Barak nears his retirement, he reflects on his background, his unique path at the Library, and on what belonging means to him.

Many of my Library of Congress colleagues who know me as an IT Specialist would be surprised to know that I received a Master’s of Library Science (MLS) from the University of Maryland College of Library and Information Services (now the College of Information) in 1991. I thought it might be interesting for others seeking technology work in libraries for me to document my trajectory as I near my retirement. Randy Pausch’s “The Last Lecture” inspired me to share this journey.  

An IT Specialist origin story begins in graduate school
